lens: Hyperscaler-grade — operational excellence, fleet-scale, lane-lifecycle hygiene
answer: ADR-0118 is a near-textbook lane-retirement at hyperscaler standards: explicit Decision, three Rejected alternatives (keep-empty, rename, full-erase), named Replacement (M01-P18 admission + projected-merge-state + conflict-kernel via ADR-0116), preserved historical lane records in both docs/ and .omc/ surfaces, supersedes ADR-0052, and IP-008 reframed status=retired with retirement-validation commands replacing acceptance commands. Workspace, Cargo.lock, registry catalog (3 entries), CHANGELOG, INDEX, ADR-0104/0107 backrefs, and evidence/agentic-pipeline JSON all updated atomically — no dangling references. The lane is correctly treated as a one-time cutover gate rather than steady-state CI; AWS/Google would similarly delete a bootstrap-only Lambda once the migration target shipped. Two hygiene gaps vs Stripe/Palantir bar: (1) no formal sunset window — lane went from Accepted to Retired same-day without a deprecation announcement period or 'last green run' metric capture; ADR-0108 sunset-lifecycle kernel exists in repo (referenced in CHANGELOG 2026-05-15) but was not applied here, creating an inconsistency in lane-retirement procedure. (2) Coverage migration is asserted ('projected-merge-state and conflict-kernel already own the replacement invariant') but not evidenced — no diff cross-reference proving M01-P18 actually exercises the four failure_modes the retired lane caught (archive-row-missing, original-still-active, archive-outside-root, live-ref-to-archived). For a one-time cleanup lane post-cutover this is acceptable; for a steady-state lane it would be blocking. IP-008 was the correct hierarchy slot per milestone>phase>impl-plan rule.
key_claims: ADR-0118 follows canonical retirement pattern (Decision, Rejected alternatives, Replacement, Verification, supersedes chain) rather than rip-and-replace
Atomic deletion: workspace members, Cargo.lock, registry/catalog (3 yaml files), backrefs in ADR-0104/0107, INDEX, CHANGELOG, and IP-008 evidence JSON all updated in one PR — zero dangling references
Lane is correctly classified as one-time cutover gate (bootstrap Lambda pattern), not steady-state CI, justifying full removal over rename
Historical traceability preserved in both docs/governance-lanes/archive-orphan.md and .omc/governance-lanes/archive-orphan.md with retired_on/retired_by frontmatter
IP-008 hierarchy placement is correct: lane is owned by M01-P08-IP-008, so retirement record lives in same IP file (milestone>phase>impl-plan compliance)
Replacement gate (M01-P18 admission + projected-merge-state + conflict-kernel) is named but not cross-referenced to the four specific failure_modes the retired lane caught
uncertainty_areas: Whether M01-P18 conflict-kernel actually catches archive-row-missing / original-still-active invariants (asserted, not evidenced in diff)
Whether the lane ever ran green in CI and produced a pre-retirement metric (no 'last green' citation in ADR-0118 Verification plan)
Whether ADR-0108 sunset-lifecycle kernel should have driven this retirement through a deprecation window rather than same-day Accepted->Retired
anti_patterns_detected: Missing sunset-window / deprecation-announcement period — ADR-0108 sunset-lifecycle automation exists in repo but was bypassed here, creating a procedure inconsistency
No pre-retirement metric captured (lane-execution count, last-green-run-date) — hyperscalers require 'data justifying it ever existed' before deletion
Replacement-coverage assertion without diff evidence — ADR-0118 claims M01-P18 owns the invariant but does not point to the specific kernel checks that subsume the four failure_modes

findings.summary: ADR-0118 skips ADR-0108 sunset-lifecycle procedure: lane went from Accepted (2026-05-12) to Retired (2026-05-16) without a documented deprecation window or sunset clause, despite repo having a dedicated sunset-lifecycle kernel landed 2026-05-15.
findings.recommended_action: Either add a _sunset frontmatter object to ADR-0118 retroactively documenting the 4-day cutover window as the de-facto sunset, OR amend ADR-0108 / the fitness-lane retirement procedure to explicitly exempt one-time-cutover lanes from the standard sunset>deprecation>removal cycle. The current PR is fine as-is but the procedure inconsistency will recur.

findings.summary: ADR-0118 asserts M01-P18 owns the replacement invariant but does not cross-reference the four specific failure_modes (archive-row-missing, original-still-active, archive-outside-root, live-ref-to-archived) to specific M01-P18 kernel checks. For a one-time lane this is acceptable, but the assertion is not evidence-backed.
findings.recommended_action: Add a Coverage-migration subsection to ADR-0118 mapping each retired failure_mode to either (a) the M01-P18 kernel that subsumes it or (b) an explicit 'no longer reachable post-cutover' justification. Three lines suffice.

findings.summary: No pre-retirement metric captured: ADR-0118 Verification plan validates removal but not 'did this lane ever produce signal'. Hyperscaler bar requires last-green-date or execution count to justify both the lane's prior existence and the safety of its removal.
findings.recommended_action: Add one bullet to Consequences or Verification: 'Lane executed N times via IP-008 P6/P7 gating, last green on YYYY-MM-DD; archived payload integrity confirmed by final run before deletion.' If no run history exists, state that explicitly.
